methods.label: Add the untouched semicircle and the outer segment
methods.explanation:
The radius is \(6\) feet. The path edge through the center divides the circle into two semicircles, one of which remains entirely grass. The other path edge cuts off an additional grassy segment beyond the path.

Let \(O\) be the center, let \(A\) and \(B\) be the points where the outer path edge meets the circle, and let \(M\) be the perpendicular foot from \(O\) to \(AB\). The path width gives \(OM=3\), and the perpendicular from the center bisects the chord. Hence
\[
AM=BM=\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=3\sqrt3,
\]
so \(AB=6\sqrt3\).

Triangle \(OMA\) has side lengths \(3,3\sqrt3,6\), the \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) ratio, with \(\angle AOM=60^\circ\). The equal triangle on the other side of \(OM\) gives \(\angle MOB=60^\circ\), so the minor sector \(AOB\) has central angle \(120^\circ\).

The grassy segment beyond \(AB\) is this sector with triangle \(OAB\) removed. Its area is
\[
\frac{120}{360}\pi(6^2)
-\frac12(6\sqrt3)(3)
=12\pi-9\sqrt3.
\]
Adding the untouched semicircle gives the full remaining grass area:
\[
\frac12\pi(6^2)+12\pi-9\sqrt3
=\boxed{30\pi-9\sqrt3}
\]
square feet, choice E.
